title: Build it badly, end to end
arc: Season two opens with a promise to Asha: a working path from the first ride event to a number on a dashboard in one week, ugly but complete. Dev is sceptical; he has seen platforms that were all plans. You build the walking skeleton: events into Kafka, raw files in the lake, a Spark job, an Airflow DAG, and the idea that ties it together, idempotency. Midweek a rerun doubles every row, and you learn why every step must be safe to run twice.
previously: Why build the whole path badly before building any part well?
Where does a ride event live between Kafka and the dashboard?
Recall: what makes a job safe to rerun?
What does an orchestrator give you that cron does not?
cliff: Dev bets it won't run end to end by Friday. Which part breaks first?
A rerun doubled every row. What was missing?
Airflow ran the job twice for one hour. Whose fault is that?
The lake is filling with tiny files. Why does that slow every query?

scenes.monday: Asha's ask: one week, one ride event, all the way to a dashboard. Dev bets you a coffee it won't run end to end by Friday. Start with why you build everything first, badly.
scenes.midweek: A rerun of last night's job doubles every row on the dashboard. Nobody noticed until Tomas did. Read and fix the hour that counts a row twice, and make the load safe to rerun.
scenes.friday: The skeleton runs end to end: Kafka, the lake, Spark and Airflow. Run it under load in the simulator, then answer Grace: forty cron jobs or one orchestrator?
